name: item_hover_highlight
description: Frozen reference behaviour for HOVER FEEDBACK while the current selection type is Item. Four facts: the highlighted unit is the WHOLE item under the cursor (never the polygon under the cursor); what is painted is the item's EDGES, one pixel wide, with the surface left untouched; the painted pixel set is bit-identical to the one the selected-item look paints, so coverage is shared and only the colour differs; and the colour is a three-state function of (selected, hovered) with the selected+hovered state DERIVED from the selection colour rather than being a fourth independent constant.
source: Frozen reference capture (isolated headless session, scripted): a five-item orthographic rig, cursor placed by injected pointer motion, every figure a pixel read on retained screenshots. Screen positions were derived by frame differencing (largest connected component) plus a two-axis least-squares fit, never by a camera model.

provenance.harness: private headless capture harness (driver, in-editor probe, offline analyser, manifest and retained screenshots live in the private tree)
provenance.notes: Colours are single exact modal values over 956 of 956 painted pixels — no anti-aliasing and no alpha, so there is nothing averaged here. The colour SOURCE was established by a preference lever, not by matching against a shipped table: each candidate scheme colour was driven onto its own RGB axis and the capture re-run, so the paint names its own source. The default-scheme numbers and the lever numbers are both recorded below and must agree with each other.

parameters.notes: drive record read from doc/tasks/0647-evidence/README.md:87; The driven parameter is the colour-scheme lever: the capture's probe carries a SPECTRAL table (atlas_itemhover_probe.py:69) driving each candidate scheme colour onto its own RGB axis, and a DEFAULTS table (:81) restoring it; the fixture's own `color_source_lever.observations` carries the same four (driven, to) pairs and the two were cross-read. The reference's preference KEYS are not reproduced -- each value is recorded under the logical name the public fixture already uses (selection_color / prehighlight_color / face_prehighlight_color / selection_fill_color), one dotted leaf per channel -- a flat list would be read back as three DISTINCT driven values of one parameter rather than as one colour. TWO THINGS A READER SHOULD KNOW: (a) the four lever observations are ONE re-run that drove all four simultaneously, split here so each cell names the colour whose paint it attributes; (b) the probe's spectral table also drove a fifth colour, the idle wireframe, to (1,1,0) purely as a lever-liveness gate -- it has no observation row in the fixture and no logical name there, so it is named here instead of being invented as a cell. The eight `cases` cells drove nothing: they are cursor placements and selections under the shipped default scheme, read as pixels. `selected_and_hovered_law.checks[1]`'s red base is the same driven value already recorded in the selection_color cell; checks[0]'s base is the shipped default, not driven.

conditions.comment: Ambient state for every figure below.
conditions.view: orthographic front, 40 px per world metre

unit.comment: The trap this rig was built for: with one item in the scene, 'the item under the cursor is lit' and 'every item is lit' render identically. Three separated items settle it, and a second probe on a DIFFERENT polygon of the same item settles the sub-item question.

paint.comment: Which pixels the highlight covers. A face-interior probe separates a surface tint from an edge draw; an interior-edge probe separates an edge draw from a silhouette-only outline. Both were taken; neither was reasoned about.

evidence.expected_full_wireframe_note: a 2x2 grid at 160 px per side: 4*160 boundary + 2*160 interior, one pixel wide

coverage_shared_with_selection.comment: The strongest form of 'it is drawn like the selected item': not the same COUNT, the same PIXELS.

colors.comment: RGB 0-255 as read from the framebuffer, and the normalised value each is exactly equal to. hover_equals_selection is the question this capture existed to answer.

reference_values_in_the_same_frames.comment: Recorded so a future run can tell a changed highlight from a changed scheme.

selected_and_hovered_law.comment: The third colour is not an independent constant and not a blend toward the pre-highlight colour. It is the selection colour brightened by a fixed amount per channel and clamped. Confirmed against TWO different selection colours, six channels, all within one 8-bit step — a single base colour could not have distinguished a brighten from a blend.

checks.note: one 8-bit step, consistent with a truncating float-to-byte conversion

refuted_alternatives.note: close on this base colour, but it predicts a prehighlight-tinted result on the red base and the red base measured a pure brighten

color_source_lever.comment: Each candidate scheme colour was driven onto its own RGB axis and the identical capture re-run. The paint then names its own source, which no amount of matching an RGB against a table can do. This also rules two candidates OUT by their total absence.

observations.conclusion: item-mode hover uses the GENERIC pre-highlight colour, not the face-specific one
nothing is filled, consistent with the zero-pixel face-interior probe

cases.comment: One row per swept condition. painted_px is measured inside that item's own footprint; a zero is as much a measurement as a non-zero.

hover_a_background_visible_unselected_la.note: a background layer pre-highlights normally; the foreground item keeps its selection colour

cursor_over_empty_space.note: measured in the gap BETWEEN two items, not off the edge of the view; and returning to the parking pixel restored the frame to zero difference three separate times, so the state is transient, not latched

several_items_along_the_ray.comment: An occluder strictly inside the occludee's footprint and 3 m closer to the camera. Exactly one item highlights and it is the front-most; the editor's own click picker independently returns that same item for that pixel.

image_plane_item_with_no_mesh.comment: An item that has no geometry at all still participates, by the same law and with the same three colours. Its border is TWO pixels wide, unlike a mesh's one-pixel edges, and its image area is never tinted.

secondary_cue_outside_the_viewport.comment: Found by a whole-frame diff rather than a pane-clipped one, which is a superset test: this is the ONLY other thing that moved. It is chrome, not the highlight, but a port that reproduces the highlight and not this is knowingly incomplete.
secondary_cue_outside_the_viewport.over_empty_viewport: offers the viewport-level inputs (pick, viewport context menu)
secondary_cue_outside_the_viewport.over_any_item: offers the item-level inputs (item context menu, area select, item properties)

controls.comment: Every one of these ran before the figures above were trusted. Without them a zero is indistinguishable from a broken probe.
controls.cursor_not_in_framebuffer_note: the two parkings are different empty pixels; the screenshot channel does not composite the cursor, so no figure above can be the cursor bitmap
